mild CHF exacerbation whose course was complicated by 
superimposed asthma exacerbation and Klebsiella UTI.
# Acute on Chronic Systolic Heart Failure w Reduced EF (45%)

Patient originally presented describing several months of 
dyspnea on exertion with PND and orthopnea occurring in last 
week prior to presentation.

Found to be in mild CHF 
exacerbation.

Etiology somewhat unclear, however per report 
there was recent re-titration of Lasix dosing (20mg to 40mg) 
with some confusion on her part.

Additionally hypertensive on 
presentation to 170s-180s systolic, albeit briefly.

Therefore 
possible contributors were medication concordance as well as 
poor BP control.

Subsequent work up with P-MIBI showing fixed inferolateral wall 
perfusion defect and hypokinesis of and mildly decreased 
approximate ejection fraction of 45%.

Given fixed defect would 
not likely benefit from revascularization.
